title: ERCP
what: A flexible tube with a camera is passed through your mouth into the first part of the small bowel. Through it, contrast dye goes into the bile and pancreatic ducts, and X-rays are taken. Stones can be removed or a small tube called a stent placed right away.
why: For stones in the bile duct, jaundice from a blocked duct, narrowed ducts, or to replace a stent.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; a hospital stay of at least one day is usually needed
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. They often need to be changed for a short time. Your doctor decides
Allergy to iodine, contrast dye, or medicines
Diabetes. Your medicines and fasting will need to be adjusted
If you are or might be pregnant

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 to 8 hours and no drinks for 2 to 4 hours before. Your doctor will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide what to take and when.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood and clotting tests are usually needed. The clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Consent
prepare.text: The procedure, its risks, and sedation will be discussed with you. Ask all your questions before you sign.

bring: Things for 1 to 2 days in hospital
steps: An IV line is put in a vein
Your throat is sprayed, and a mouth guard is put in
Medicine is given, and you fall asleep or doze
You usually lie on your stomach
The doctor passes the tube through your mouth into the bowel and finds the duct opening
Contrast is given and X-rays are taken
If needed, stones are removed or a stent is placed
feel: During the procedure, you usually sleep and feel nothing
Afterward, your throat may be sore and your belly bloated
You will feel sleepy for a while
after: You stay under a doctor's watch
You can eat and drink when the doctor allows, usually not right away
After sedation, do not drive that day
The doctor will explain the results after the procedure
red_flags: Severe pain in the belly or back: tell the doctor right away. At home, call emergency services
Vomiting blood or black stools: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), chills, or yellowing skin: call your doctor or emergency services
Trouble breathing or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: It is an endoscopic procedure with no cuts. But it is more complex than a regular upper endoscopy, so you are watched in hospital.
Most often, inflammation of the pancreas after the procedure. That is why the doctor watches your pain and blood tests.

faq.q: Will the stent need to be changed?
faq.a: If a stent was placed, your doctor will tell you if and when it needs to be removed or replaced.

reminders.text: ERCP tomorrow. Check the time after which you cannot eat or drink, and pack for the hospital.
